title: Governance and Learning Systems Datasheet
purpose: Comparative framework for representing governance arrangements and learning systems as SYSTOS system objects. A named form is not treated as proof of a desired outcome.

comparison_dimensions.governance: Who decides, by what rules, with what accountability and feedback?
comparison_dimensions.learning: How does a person or group acquire, retain, apply, and revise knowledge or skill?

comparison_dimensions.governance: Institutional performance, accountability, service delivery, participation, rights, conflict resolution, policy outcomes.
comparison_dimensions.learning: Retention, transfer, performance, engagement, skill acquisition, delayed recall, quality of application.

comparison_dimensions.governance: A named constitutional form automatically produces good governance.
comparison_dimensions.learning: A popular teaching method automatically produces durable learning.

comparison_dimensions.governance: Compare mechanisms and outcomes in context; separate formal rules from actual practice.
comparison_dimensions.learning: Combine methods; match method to task, learner, time horizon, and desired outcome.

systos_integration.governance: Represent each governance arrangement as a system with actors, rules, resources, flows, failure modes, reforms, and temporal variants.
systos_integration.learning: Represent each learning system as an institution/practice with methods, roles, resources, outcomes, evidence, and contexts.
systos_integration.epistemic_rule: Separate descriptive mechanism, observed outcome, evidence, interpretation, and normative judgment.
systos_integration.relationship_rule: Governance and learning systems may connect to other SYSTOS records through first-class relationships carrying provenance, confidence, temporal scope, context, and evidence.
